subject.title: bug(cost): mid-session writes to bootstrap-injected files trigger cacheWrite spiral on long agentic sessions; bootstrap-cache.ts shipped for #43532 is content-equality, not session-freeze

question: Should OpenClaw solve this by adding opt-in session-frozen bootstrap snapshots, adding configurable dynamic bootstrap files, or keeping live refresh and documenting the cacheWrite tradeoff?
rationale: Each viable path creates or confirms a durable prompt-cache/session-state contract: freezing bootstrap content can hide live file edits from the system prompt, while dynamic-file configuration adds a new compatibility-sensitive config surface.

options.title: Prioritize configurable dynamic files
options.body: Add a narrow `bootstrapDynamicFiles`-style surface, aligned with the open dynamic-file tracker, so volatile files can move below the cache boundary while normal live bootstrap visibility remains available.

options.title: Add opt-in session freeze
options.body: Add a `bootstrapFreezeMode: "session"`-style mode with unchanged live defaults and tests proving file-tool reads remain live while system-prompt bootstrap content stays frozen for the session.

options.title: Document live refresh only
options.body: Keep the current content-equality refresh behavior and update prompt-caching/model-selection docs to warn that volatile bootstrap files above the boundary can drive cacheWrite spikes.

recommendation.title: Prioritize configurable dynamic files
recommendation.body: Add a narrow `bootstrapDynamicFiles`-style surface, aligned with the open dynamic-file tracker, so volatile files can move below the cache boundary while normal live bootstrap visibility remains available.

likelyOwner.reason: The earlier session-freeze close and the original bootstrap snapshot cache history make `steipete` the best available owner for deciding whether that contract should change.
